items.content_html:
Follow-up to commit f20cd90 (where log() was defined for missing argument errors).

Options like --file and --attr properly check if an argument was provided:

--file|-f)
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
        log "$0: '$i' requires an argument"
        exit 1
    fi

However, other flags consuming arguments (--root, --channel, --system, --flake, --max-jobs) unconditionally ran shift 1. When invoked with a trailing flag without an argument (e.g. nixos-install --root), shift 1 fails on an empty parameter list, causing bash to silently abort with exit code 1 under set -e.

Changes:

  • Add [ -z "$1" ] checks before shifting for --max-jobs, --root, --system, --flake, and --channel.
  • Report $0: '$i' requires an argument via log and exit with 1.

Testing:

$ nix-build -A nixos-install
/nix/store/znqsv634klrargdgha5nz6j390cxmjv2-nixos-install

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --root
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--root' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --channel
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--channel' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-install --max-jobs
./result/bin/nixos-install: '--max-jobs' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

When nixos-enter is invoked with an option requiring an argument (--root, --system, or --command/-c) as the final parameter, the script unconditionally executes shift 1 on an empty parameter list:

$ sudo nixos-enter --root
$ echo $?
1

Because shift 1 fails on the empty positional parameters and set -e is active, the script silently aborts with exit code 1 without providing any diagnostic message to the user.

Changes:

  • Add a check [ -z "$1" ] before shifting for --root, --system, and --command/-c
  • Output $0: '$i' requires an argument to stderr and exit with 1

Testing:

Verified manually with ./result/bin/nixos-enter:

$ ./result/bin/nixos-enter --root
./result/bin/nixos-enter: '--root' requires an argument
$ echo $?
1

$ ./result/bin/nixos-enter -c
./result/bin/nixos-enter: '-c' requires an argument
$ echo $?

items.content_html:
Depends on #555814 (t3code-cli).

Adds a NixOS module for T3 Code:

services.t3code.enable = true;

Upstream ships t3 service install, which turns on linger, installs a pinned t3 from npm into ~/.t3/runtime, and runs it under a launcher that updates itself. This module installs the same kind of systemd user unit, but runs t3 serve straight from the store, with upstream's kill and OOM settings. Remote self-update requests are disabled, because the server isn't running under upstream's launcher.

  • user defaults to t3code, which is created when left at the default. Set it to your own account to let agents work on your repositories and provider credentials. State lives in that user's ~/.t3.
  • The unit is a user unit (ConditionUser = cfg.user) with linger enabled, so it starts at boot and runs inside the user's systemd manager. That keeps upstream's per-agent systemd-run --user --scope scopes and their memory limits. Logs: journalctl _SYSTEMD_USER_UNIT=t3code.service.
  • cfg.package is installed for the user. Pair a client with t3 auth pairing create as that user. Like upstream, t3 serve also prints a one-time admin pairing token (expires after 5 minutes) on start, so it ends up in the user journal.
  • host defaults to 127.0.0.1 (same as upstream) and port to 3773. openFirewall is available for remote access; anyone reaching a non-loopback address can drive agents as user.
  • Telemetry (PostHog) is off by default through T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED = mkDefault "false".
  • Provider CLIs come from the existing package overrides, e.g. package = pkgs.t3code-cli.override { enableClaude = true; }.

The VM test waits for user@1000.service before any login, checks that the server has XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and that a scope can be started in app-t3code-agents.slice, waits for the "server is ready" log line (upstream accepts TCP connections before its HTTP handler is attached: pingdotgg/t3code#12215), and runs t3 auth pairing create through PATH.

cc @iamanaws @qweered as t3code maintainers: this adds passthru.tests.nixos to the package. Happy to add you as module co-maintainers if you want to be.

AI disclosure: the module and test were drafted with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) and reviewed by me. The commits carry Assisted-by: trailers. The upstream behavior relied on here (unit template, default bind address, telemetry switch, startup pairing token, agent scopes, self-update gating, startup race) was checked against the shipped bundle and reproduced in the VM test.

items.content_html:
TL;DR: The PR forces deterministic ordering between rw-etc and /rw-etc

Context

My / is on tmpfs. Historically, I've kept the entire /etc folder on persistent storage via a bind mount to a persisted location (/etc -> /persist/etc). This doesn't work with system.etc.overlay since it requires it's own mount on /etc to work, locking you out completely from your machine, almost identically to #319524

Fix

The fix, I've found, is to persist .rw-etc instead which seems to be where mutable files go. However, I can see that ATM the rw-etc unit relies on / only for ordering. This won't work properly if you have /.rw-etc as a separate mount which is required for those follow an root level 'impermanence' setup like myself since there's technically nothing stopping rw-etc running before the /.rw-etc mount gets created first. Thus, I've added it to the RequiresMountsFor
